results.correct_value: Retreat by reversing the boot path down Box Ridge to the Rachel Lake Trail
results.evidence: Published route descriptions of Hibox all describe one out-and-back line: Rachel Lake Trail to the first avalanche clearing, the climbers' boot path up Box Ridge, and back the same way; none sends a party to Rampart Lakes, which lies west beyond Rachel Lake and is the base for Alta Mountain. The row's own descent and descent_text also reverse the boot path to the Rachel Lake Trail. The partner-requirements approach line also named the Rampart Lakes trail, which this route never reaches.

patches.value: Reverse the boot path down Box Ridge to the Rachel Lake Trail and walk out the trail to the trailhead.

results.correct_value: About 7 miles round trip (about 3.5 miles / 5.6 km one way)
results.evidence: The itinerary said ~10 mi round trip, partner requirements ~6.7 mi round trip, and dist_km / the approach variant 5 mi (8 km) one way. One route description gives 3.5 miles and 3,800 ft to the summit; another gives 7 miles round trip and 3,800 ft; a trail listing gives about 7.3 miles out and back (a club listing says 8 miles). The trail leg is ~2 miles and the boot path is short and steep, so ~3.5 miles one way fits.

results.fact: 'Rampart Lakes' waypoint on the Hibox route
results.evidence: The waypoint list includes a 'Rampart Lakes' Junction pin west of Rachel Lake, which the Hibox line (boot path leaving the trail ~2 mi in, below Rachel Lake) never passes. Removing or moving a pin is outside this pass, so it is only flagged.

results.fact: Total elevation gain/loss for the route
results.evidence: Measured round trips to Huckleberry via the PCT from Snoqualmie Pass report 21.6 mi with 5,850 ft gained and lost, ~23 mi with ~6,800 ft, and 25 mi with 7,700 ft; the PCT rolls over Kendall Pass and around Alaska Mountain, so 3,377 ft (essentially the net trailhead-to-summit rise) is far too low. The row's own itinerary (2,700 + 3,620) and totalNote (~6,300 ft) sit inside the published range, so gain_ft/loss_ft go to 6,320 and day 2 loss is corrected so total loss equals total gain (100 + 6,220). The approach sentence that called ~6,320 ft the gain to Huckleberry Flats alone is corrected.

results.fact: Total cumulative elevation gain for the route
results.evidence: A measured East Ridge trip from Snoqualmie Pass with a Ridge Lake camp reports 21.6 mi and 5,850 ft gained and lost; other PCT-approach trips report ~6,800 ft (23 mi) and 7,700 ft (25 mi, East Ridge). All exceed 4,600 ft, which is the one-way gain to the base of the ridge (2,700 ft to camp plus ~1,900 ft to the base, as the row's approach says), not the round trip. The itinerary's ~5,800+ ft agrees; the approach variant's 4,600 ft is the one-way approach figure and is left alone.

results.fact: pitch count on the South Ridge
results.evidence: Published counts genuinely differ: a widely used route listing gives 4 pitches over 300 ft (the source of this row's 91 m length), a route description gives three pitches, and a trip report climbed it in 3 while noting the standard is 4. results.correct_value: Rappel the route from the three-bolt summit anchor: three rappels on two 60 m ropes, four on a single 60 m
results.evidence: A route description recommends rappelling the climbing line rather than downclimbing, in four raps on a single 60 m rope from the three-bolt summit anchor; a route listing notes a 60 m falls about 15 ft short from the pitch-3 anchor and gives two-rope rappel guidance; a club trip report describes three rappels on two 60 m ropes. The descent field and itinerary (downclimb with one short rappel) were the outliers, and descent_text and the summit waypoint also put three rappels on a single 60 m rope, contradicting the row's own rappels and rappel_count_note.

results.fact: rappel sequence/count on the shared South Ridge descent
results.evidence: Both sequences are documented by real two-rope parties: one East Ridge trip report rappelled single to the bolts, double to the ledge, single to the top of pitch 1 and double to the base (four, matching the descent field); another did one single and two double-rope rappels (three); a two-rope South Ridge party did it in two. The count depends on the party and conditions rather than one standard; the rendered descent_text (three on two ropes, four on one) sits in that range and the hidden descent field describes a real four-rappel variant. No single value is established by two agreeing sources, so no patch.

results.fact: Which approach and which ridge this 'South Route' actually climbs
results.correct_value: The scramble finishes on the west ridge, drops to a notch, and takes a ramp below the summit block to the north ridge; there is no south-ridge line
results.evidence: The peak's reference entry gives the easiest route as class 2-3 on the North Ridge. Trip reports describe ascending talus to Iron Cap's west ridge from the Chetwoot / Iron Cap Lake side, a short 3rd-class downclimb into a notch, then a wide ramp below the summit meeting the broad north ridge, and call the west ridge easy class 3; none describes a south-ridge route. The ridge labels (face, overview, beta, climbing_route[0], the approach's last step, descent_text, bail) are corrected. NOT resolved here: which approach the row describes (Middle Fork / Dutch Miller Gap / Williams Lake in approach, itinerary, timing and waypoints versus a West Fork Foss / Chetwoot Lake approach in beta, bail, rope_note and the Dingford Creek waypoint note, which names West Fork Foss lakes that are not reached from Dingford Creek). The aspect 'S' likely also follows the wrong ridge but was left.
